In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-monitoring-operator/pull/2889):

>Apply the same Phase 1 rules as metricsServer: when cluster-monitoring-config does not define alertmanagerMain, merge spec.alertmanagerConfig from the ClusterMonitoring CR (deploymentMode Disabled/DefaultConfig/CustomConfig and customConfig fields). ConfigMap values still win when alertmanagerMain is present.
>
>Leave AlertmanagerMainConfig unset in applyDefaults until merge, default it in EnsureSafeDefaults, and initialize a non-nil struct in NewFactory for code paths that build manifests without MergeClusterMonitoringCRD.
>
>Share CRD []ContainerResource → corev1.ResourceRequirements conversion via containerResourcesFromCRD for metrics server and alertmanager.
>
>Add unit tests (config_merge_test) and e2e tests for CR-driven settings and ConfigMap vs CR precedence.
>
>

<details>
<summary>📝 Walkthrough</summary>

## Walkthrough

The PR extends ClusterMonitoring config merge to also merge PrometheusOperatorConfig and AlertmanagerConfig. It adds predicates to detect empty CR specs, introduces CR→manifest log level conversion, and implements a shared `containerResourcesFromCRD` helper reused by MetricsServer and Alertmanager merging. MetricsServer merging is refactored to use the shared helper. Alertmanager merging branches on `DeploymentMode` (`Disabled` sets `Enabled=false`, `Default` leaves `Enabled` unset, `Custom` copies fields, converts secret strings, and transforms a `VolumeClaimTemplate` PVC into a Prometheus-operator `EmbeddedPersistentVolumeClaim` with `TypeMeta` and embedded metadata). Unit and e2e tests covering these behaviors were added.

## Estimated code review effort

🎯 3 (Moderate) | ⏱️ ~25 minutes

</details>

🧹 Nitpick comments (1)
pkg/manifests/config_merge.go (1)
`228-242`: **Consider whether PVC annotations should be copied.** The conversion copies `Name`, `Labels`, and `Spec`, but omits `Annotations`. If users specify annotations on the `VolumeClaimTemplate` in the CR (e.g., for storage class hints or custom metadata), they would be lost.
♻️ Proposed fix to include annotations ```diff func persistentVolumeClaimToEmbedded(pvc *v1.PersistentVolumeClaim) *monv1.EmbeddedPersistentVolumeClaim { if pvc == nil { return nil } em := &monv1.EmbeddedPersistentVolumeClaim{ TypeMeta: metav1.TypeMeta{ APIVersion: v1.SchemeGroupVersion.String(), Kind: "PersistentVolumeClaim", }, } em.EmbeddedObjectMetadata.Name = pvc.Name em.EmbeddedObjectMetadata.Labels = pvc.Labels + em.EmbeddedObjectMetadata.Annotations = pvc.Annotations em.Spec = pvc.Spec return em } ```
---

`90-94`: **Consider documenting the DeploymentMode requirement.** The `clusterMonitoringAlertmanagerSpecEmpty` predicate only checks `DeploymentMode`, which means any `CustomConfig` fields set without a `DeploymentMode` will be silently ignored. While this is intentional (requiring explicit deployment intent), a brief comment explaining this design decision would help future maintainers.
pkg/manifests/config_merge_test.go (1)
`192-237`: **Good test coverage, consider adding DefaultConfig mode test.** The tests cover `CustomConfig` and `Disabled` modes well. Consider adding a test case for `DefaultConfig` mode to verify that `Enabled` remains `nil` (which evaluates to `true` via `IsEnabled()`), ensuring the platform defaults behavior is explicitly validated.
📝 Suggested additional test case ```go t.Run("CR DefaultConfig leaves Enabled nil", func(t *testing.T) { cm := &configv1alpha1.ClusterMonitoring{ Spec: configv1alpha1.ClusterMonitoringSpec{ AlertmanagerConfig: configv1alpha1.AlertmanagerConfig{ DeploymentMode: configv1alpha1.AlertManagerDeployModeDefaultConfig, }, }, } c, err := NewConfigFromStringAndClusterMonitoringResource("{}", cm) require.NoError(t, err) require.NotNil(t, c.ClusterMonitoringConfiguration.AlertmanagerMainConfig) require.Nil(t, c.ClusterMonitoringConfiguration.AlertmanagerMainConfig.Enabled) require.True(t, c.ClusterMonitoringConfiguration.AlertmanagerMainConfig.IsEnabled()) }) ```
test/e2e/cluster_monitoring_test.go (1)
`454-456`: **Consider cleanup ordering for test stability.** The cleanup deletes the ConfigMap (line 455), but the CR cleanup (lines 488-492) runs afterward and updates the CR. Since Go's `t.Cleanup` functions run in LIFO order, the CR update happens first, then the ConfigMap deletion. This ordering should be fine, but be aware that if the CR update depends on ConfigMap state, test teardown order matters.
